title: Spectroscopy and chromatography
unit: A2 (unit number not stated in text; inferred from topic)

questions.question: Five C5H10O2 isomers: A is straight-chain and reacts with Na2CO3 to give CO2; B has only two singlet peaks in high-resolution 1H NMR; C has a chiral centre; D has no chiral centre. All of A-D react with Na2CO3 to give CO2. Give the structures of A, B, C and D.
questions.answer: A = CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH (pentanoic acid); B = (CH3)3CCOOH (2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid); C = CH3CH2CH(CH3)COOH (2-methylbutanoic acid); D = (CH3)2CHCH2COOH (3-methylbutanoic acid)
steps: Reaction with Na2CO3 giving CO2 shows each isomer is a carboxylic acid (-COOH)
A is straight-chain, so the acid is pentanoic acid
B has two singlets only: 9H (tert-butyl) and 1H (COOH), so B is (CH3)3CCOOH
C has a chiral centre (a C bonded to four different groups), so C is 2-methylbutanoic acid
D has no chiral centre and is not straight-chain or B, so D is 3-methylbutanoic acid

questions.question: Isomer E contains an ether group and a ketone group and its low-resolution 1H NMR spectrum has four peaks. Complete the table for the four labelled hydrogen environments, including the splitting pattern in high-resolution spectrum.
questions.answer: b: relative area 2, shift 2.9-4.2 ppm, triplet; c: relative area 2, shift 2.2-2.7 ppm, triplet; d: relative area 3, shift 2.2-2.7 ppm, singlet
steps: Relative peak area = number of H in each environment: CH3-O (a) = 3, O-CH2 (b) = 2, CH2-C=O (c) = 2, CH3-C=O (d) = 3
Peak b (O-CH2) is next to the CH2 (c) only, so n = 2 neighbours gives n+1 = 3: a triplet; its shift is 2.9-4.2 ppm because the carbon is bonded to oxygen
Peak c (CH2-C=O) is next to the CH2 (b) only, so it is also a triplet; being next to C=O it comes at about 2.2-2.7 ppm
Peak d (CH3-C=O) has no hydrogens on the neighbouring carbonyl carbon, so it is a singlet, area 3, at about 2.2-2.7 ppm

questions.question: State the number of peaks in the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of isomer E.
questions.answer: 5 peaks
steps: Each different carbon environment gives one peak in the 13C NMR spectrum
E is CH3-O-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-CH3, and none of its five carbons is equivalent to another: CH3O, OCH2, CH2C=O, C=O and CH3C=O
So there are 5 peaks

questions.question: Isomer F is a neutral ester that smells of pears, formed from compounds V and W with conc. H2SO4. V has an IR absorption at 1720 cm-1 and a broad absorption around 3050 cm-1. W can be formed directly from propanal. Identify V, W and F and justify.
questions.answer: V = ethanoic acid (CH3COOH); W = propan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2OH); F = propyl ethanoate (CH3COOCH2CH2CH3)
steps: 1720 cm-1 is a C=O stretch and the broad band near 3050 cm-1 is O-H, so V is a carboxylic acid
F is neutral and formed from an acid plus an alcohol, so it is an ester and W is an alcohol
Propanal is reduced to a primary alcohol, so W is propan-1-ol
The pear-smelling ester from ethanoic acid and propan-1-ol is propyl ethanoate, so V is ethanoic acid

questions.question: State the conditions and reagent needed to form compound W (propan-1-ol) from propanal.
questions.answer: Reducing agent NaBH4 in aqueous or ethanolic solution at room temperature (LiAlH4 in dry ether, followed by dilute acid, also works)
steps: Propanal is an aldehyde and is reduced to a primary alcohol
A hydride reducing agent is needed, such as NaBH4 (or LiAlH4)
NaBH4 works in aqueous or ethanolic solution at room temperature
LiAlH4 needs dry ether and then dilute acid to work up the product

questions.question: State the role of concentrated sulfuric acid in the formation of ester F.
questions.answer: Acts as a catalyst (and absorbs the water formed, shifting the equilibrium to the right)
steps: Esterification between an acid and an alcohol is slow without a catalyst
H2SO4 protonates the carboxylic acid C=O, making its carbon more electrophilic
It also absorbs the water produced, which shifts the equilibrium towards the ester

questions.question: State which of isomers A, E and F has the highest boiling temperature and justify it.
questions.answer: A (pentanoic acid) has the highest boiling temperature because it forms hydrogen-bonded dimers
steps: A is a carboxylic acid with an O-H group, so it forms hydrogen bonds between molecules
Hydrogen bonds are the strongest intermolecular force of the three
E and F have no O-H group, so they only have permanent dipole-dipole forces and London forces
A also has a comparable molar mass to E and F (all C5H10O2 or 102), so hydrogen bonding decides the order

questions.question: Label the hydrogen environments w, x, y and z on the displayed formula of ethyl 3-oxobutanoate to match the four peaks in its 1H NMR spectrum.
questions.answer: w = the OCH2 hydrogens of the ethyl group; x = the COCH2CO hydrogens; y = the CH3 of CH3CO; z = the CH3 of the ethyl group (CH2CH3)
steps: w (about 4.2 ppm, quartet): the CH2 bonded to the ester oxygen, deshielded by O and split by the 3 H of the neighbouring CH3
x (about 3.5 ppm, singlet): the CH2 between the ketone C=O and the ester C=O, which has no hydrogens on adjacent carbons
y (about 2.3 ppm, singlet, tallest peak so 3H): the CH3 attached to the ketone C=O
z (about 1.3 ppm, triplet): the CH3 of the ethyl group, split by the 2 H of the neighbouring OCH2

questions.question: Explain the splitting patterns of the peaks at 4.2 ppm and 1.3 ppm in the 1H NMR spectrum of ethyl 3-oxobutanoate (CH3COCH2COOCH2CH3).
questions.answer: The 4.2 ppm peak (OCH2) is a quartet and the 1.3 ppm peak (CH3) is a triplet, from the ethyl group
steps: The OCH2 protons at 4.2 ppm have 3 equivalent neighbouring protons on the CH3
The n+1 rule gives 3 + 1 = 4 peaks, a quartet
The CH3 protons at 1.3 ppm have 2 neighbouring protons on the OCH2
The n+1 rule gives 2 + 1 = 3 peaks, a triplet

questions.question: Draw an isomer of ethyl 3-oxobutanoate (C6H10O3) that contains a carboxylic acid and a ketone group and has only four peaks in its 13C NMR spectrum.
questions.answer: (CH3)3C-CO-COOH (3,3-dimethyl-2-oxobutanoic acid)
steps: The isomer must have a -COOH group and a ketone C=O, and be C6H10O3
(CH3)3C-CO-COOH has the right formula (C6H10O3) and contains both groups
Its carbons are: three equivalent CH3, the quaternary C, the ketone C and the COOH carbon
That gives 4 distinct 13C environments, as required

questions.question: Complete a diagram of a thin-layer chromatogram for ethyl 3-oxobutanoate (Rf = 0.45 in ethoxyethane and hexane), including appropriate labels.
questions.answer: A rectangle showing a labelled baseline near the bottom, a labelled solvent front near the top, and one spot labelled ethyl 3-oxobutanoate at 0.45 of the distance from baseline to solvent front
steps: Draw a horizontal start (origin) line near the bottom and label it baseline; the solvent front line near the top should also be labelled
Draw one spot for ethyl 3-oxobutanoate (a single compound gives one spot) and label it
Position the spot so that its distance from the baseline is 0.45 x the distance from the baseline to the solvent front, e.g. 4.5 cm up if the solvent front is 10 cm from the baseline
Rf = distance moved by spot / distance moved by solvent front = 0.45

questions.question: Explain why the Rf value of ethyl 3-oxobutanoate is much lower than 0.45 when just hexane is used as the solvent.
questions.answer: Hexane is non-polar, so the polar ester binds strongly to the polar stationary phase and moves less far
steps: Ethyl 3-oxobutanoate is a polar molecule (ester and ketone groups)
The stationary phase (silica or alumina) is polar
Hexane is non-polar, so it cannot carry the polar ester well and the ester stays on the stationary phase
A more polar mobile phase (ethoxyethane and hexane) competes better, so it moves further and gives Rf 0.45

questions.question: Y (C8H16O2) contains 66.7% C, 11.1% H and 22.2% O by mass. Show that these data are consistent with its molecular formula.
questions.answer: C8H16O2 has M = 144.2 with %C = 66.6, %H = 11.2, %O = 22.2, which matches the data
steps: %O = 32.00 / 144.2 x 100 = 22.2%, which agrees with the given data

questions.question: Give the IUPAC name of ester Y from its structure shown in the question.
questions.answer: 2,2-dimethylpropyl propanoate
steps: The part from the acid is CH3CH2C(=O)-, three carbons, so the ester is a propanoate
The part from the alcohol is -CH2C(CH3)3: a propyl chain (three carbons) with two methyl groups on carbon 2, so it is 2,2-dimethylpropyl
The alkyl group is named first and the acid part second: 2,2-dimethylpropyl propanoate (C8H16O2)

questions.question: Draw the structures of two organic compounds that react together to form ester Y.
questions.answer: Propanoic acid, CH3CH2COOH, and 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol, (CH3)3CCH2OH (an acid chloride such as propanoyl chloride could replace the acid)
steps: Break the ester C-O single bond: the C=O side becomes the carboxylic acid CH3CH2COOH
The O-CH2C(CH3)3 side becomes the alcohol HOCH2C(CH3)3, 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol
Esterification of these two with a strong acid catalyst (conc. H2SO4) and heat gives Y plus water

questions.question: Label the three remaining hydrogen environments B, C and D on the structure of ester Y.
questions.answer: B = the CH2 of the ethyl group (next to C=O); C = the OCH2; D = the three equivalent CH3 groups on the quaternary carbon, linked as one environment
steps: A (given) is the CH3 of the ethyl group
B labels the CH2 between the CH3 and the C=O
C labels the CH2 bonded to the ester oxygen
D labels all three CH3 groups on the C(CH3)3 carbon, because they are equivalent (one label, circled together)

questions.question: Complete the table of data from the high-resolution 1H NMR spectrum of ester Y.
questions.answer: B: quartet, relative area 2; C: singlet, relative area 2; D: singlet, relative area 9
steps: B (CH2 of ethyl) has three neighbouring H on the CH3 (A), so n + 1 = 4: a quartet, area 2
C (OCH2) is bonded to the quaternary carbon, which has no H, so there is no splitting: a singlet, area 2
D (3 x CH3 on the quaternary carbon) has no H on the adjacent carbon: a singlet, area 9 (3 x 3 H)
Check: total area 3 + 2 + 2 + 9 = 16, matching the 16 H in C8H16O2

questions.question: A spot of an amino acid has moved 42 mm from the baseline. Its Rf value is 0.62. What is the distance moved by the solvent? Options: A 680 mm, B 68 mm, C 42 mm, D 26 mm.
questions.answer: B (68 mm)
steps: Rf = distance moved by spot / distance moved by solvent
0.62 = 42 mm / distance of solvent
Distance of solvent = 42 / 0.62 = 67.7 mm, which is 68 mm

questions.question: In gas chromatography, which of these would be the most suitable carrier gas? Options: A argon, B hydrogen, C methane, D oxygen.
questions.answer: A (argon)
steps: The carrier gas is the mobile phase and must be chemically inert
Oxygen is reactive and would oxidise the sample
Argon is an inert noble gas, so it does not react with the sample
Hydrogen and methane are flammable, so argon is the most suitable choice

questions.question: A component in a TLC mixture has Rf = 0.92. What can be deduced about its attractions to the stationary and mobile phases? (Answer options are shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: D: weak attraction to the stationary phase and strong attraction to the mobile phase
steps: Rf = distance moved by component / distance moved by solvent, so Rf = 0.92 means the component travelled almost as far as the solvent front
It therefore spent most of its time dissolved in the mobile phase: strong attraction to the mobile phase
It was held only weakly by the stationary phase, so option D

questions.question: Give the molecular formula of menthone from its skeletal formula.
questions.answer: C10H18O
steps: Count carbons: 6 in the ring, 1 in the methyl group and 3 in the propan-2-yl (isopropyl) group = 10 C
Hydrogens: ring CH2 x 3 = 6, ring CH x 2 = 2, CH3 = 3, isopropyl CH(CH3)2 = 7, giving 6 + 2 + 3 + 7 = 18 H
The C=O gives 1 O, so the formula is C10H18O

questions.question: Draw the mechanism for the reaction of ethanal with HCN in the presence of cyanide ions to form 2-hydroxypropanenitrile, including curly arrows, lone pairs and dipoles.
questions.answer: Nucleophilic addition: CN- attacks the delta+ carbonyl carbon, the C=O bond breaks onto O, then the alkoxide takes H+ from HCN to regenerate CN-
steps: The C=O bond is polar, so the carbonyl C is delta+ and the O is delta-
Lone pair on CN- attacks the delta+ carbon, curly arrow from the lone pair to C
The C=O pi bond breaks, curly arrow from the C=O bond onto O, giving an alkoxide ion
The alkoxide takes H+ from HCN (curly arrow from H-CN bond onto O), giving the product and regenerating CN-

questions.question: Carbonyl compound F (C6H12O) reacts with iodine in alkaline solution to give a pale yellow precipitate. Give the name or formula of the group identified by this test.
questions.answer: The CH3CO- (methyl ketone) group, i.e. -COCH3
steps: Iodine in alkaline solution gives a yellow precipitate of CHI3 (iodoform)
This test is positive only for a CH3CO- group bonded to carbon
So F contains a methyl ketone group, -COCH3

questions.question: Draw the skeletal formulae of the four possible structures of carbonyl compound F (C6H12O) that contain a CH3CO group.
questions.answer: Hexan-2-one; 4-methylpentan-2-one; 3-methylpentan-2-one; 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-one
steps: F is a C6H12O carbonyl with a CH3CO- group, so it is a methyl ketone
The C5 chain after C(=O)CH3 can have the remaining three carbons arranged in four ways
CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH3 (hexan-2-one) and CH3COCH2CH(CH3)2 (4-methylpentan-2-one)
CH3COCH(CH3)CH2CH3 (3-methylpentan-2-one) and CH3COC(CH3)3 (3,3-dimethylbutan-2-one)

questions.question: The 13C NMR spectrum of F has four peaks. Identify F by drawing its displayed formula and label the carbon environments responsible for the four peaks.
questions.answer: F = 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-one, (CH3)3C-CO-CH3, with four carbon environments
steps: Of the four candidate methyl ketones, only (CH3)3C-CO-CH3 has symmetry giving four peaks
Peak 1: the C=O carbon (about 200-210 ppm)
Peak 2: the quaternary C bonded to three CH3 groups (about 40-50 ppm)
Peak 3: the three equivalent CH3 groups of the tert-butyl group; Peak 4: the CH3 next to C=O

questions.question: Explain, in terms of all the intermolecular forces involved, why butanal has a higher boiling temperature than pentane but a lower boiling temperature than propanoic acid.
questions.answer: Butanal has permanent dipole-dipole forces (C=O) in addition to London forces, so it boils higher than pentane (same Mr); propanoic acid has hydrogen bonding, so it boils higher than butanal
steps: Pentane (Mr 72) has only London (instantaneous dipole-induced dipole) forces
Butanal (Mr 72) has the same London forces plus permanent dipole-dipole forces from its polar C=O group
Stronger intermolecular forces need more energy to separate molecules, so butanal boils higher than pentane
Propanoic acid has an O-H group, so it forms hydrogen bonds (in dimers) that are stronger than dipole-dipole forces
So propanoic acid boils higher than butanal, which has no O-H group and only dipole-dipole forces

questions.question: Give a reason why lactic acid, CH3CH(OH)COOH, shows optical isomerism.
questions.answer: It has a chiral carbon atom (chiral centre) bonded to four different groups
steps: The central C is bonded to H, OH, CH3 and COOH
These four groups are all different, so the carbon is a chiral centre
The molecule and its mirror image are non-superimposable (enantiomers)

questions.question: Give a reason why a laboratory sample of lactic acid does not rotate the plane of plane-polarised light.
questions.answer: The sample is a racemic mixture: equal amounts of the two enantiomers, whose rotations cancel
steps: Each enantiomer rotates plane-polarised light by the same amount in opposite directions
A laboratory sample is made from achiral reagents and contains equal amounts of both enantiomers
The two equal and opposite rotations cancel, so there is no net rotation

questions.question: Give the structure of the organic product formed when lactic acid reacts with concentrated phosphoric(V) acid, H3PO4.
questions.answer: CH2=CHCOOH (prop-2-enoic acid, by dehydration)
steps: Concentrated H3PO4 is a dehydrating acid for alcohols
Lactic acid loses H2O from the -OH and adjacent H, forming a C=C double bond
The product is CH2=CHCOOH (prop-2-enoic acid)

questions.question: A reaction scheme involving butanoic acid is shown. Identify X, Y and Z by name or formula.
questions.answer: X = butan-1-ol, CH3CH2CH2CH2OH; Y = phosphorus(V) chloride, PCl5 (or SOCl2); Z = N-methylbutanamide, CH3CH2CH2CONHCH3
steps: Acidified K2Cr2O7 heated under reflux oxidises a primary alcohol fully to a carboxylic acid, so X is butan-1-ol
A carboxylic acid is converted into an acyl chloride by PCl5 (or PCl3 or SOCl2), so Y is PCl5
Butanoyl chloride reacts with methylamine (nucleophilic addition-elimination), losing HCl, to give the N-substituted amide CH3CH2CH2CONHCH3

questions.question: Give the structures of the two monomers that could form the polyester whose repeat unit is shown.
questions.answer: Monomer 1: ethane-1,2-diol, HOCH2CH2OH; Monomer 2: (E)-but-2-enedioic acid, HOOCCH=CHCOOH
steps: A polyester repeat unit contains ester links -O-C(=O)-, formed from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid (condensation, losing water)
The -OCH2CH2O- section comes from ethane-1,2-diol
The -C(=O)CH=CHC(=O)- section comes from but-2-enedioic acid (drawn with the H atoms trans, so fumaric acid); the acid chloride or diacyl dichloride would also do

questions.question: Compound E contains C, H and O only, has five carbon atoms and a molecular ion peak at m/z = 102.0678. Deduce its molecular formula.
questions.answer: C5H10O2
steps: This matches the molecular ion peak given
So the molecular formula is C5H10O2

questions.question: Aqueous sodium hydrogencarbonate is added to compound E and no effervescence occurs. State what can be deduced.
questions.answer: E is not a carboxylic acid (no COOH group)
steps: Carboxylic acids react with NaHCO3 to release CO2 (effervescence)
No effervescence means E does not contain a -COOH group

questions.question: The IR spectrum of E has an absorption in the range 1750-1735 cm-1. Name the functional group in E.
questions.answer: Ester (C=O in an ester group)
steps: The C=O stretch of an ester absorbs at about 1735-1750 cm-1
E is C5H10O2 with a C=O and no COOH, so the functional group is an ester

questions.question: Data from the high-resolution 1H NMR spectrum of E is shown. Deduce the structure of E and justify it by labelling the protons responsible for each peak.
questions.answer: E = propyl ethanoate, CH3COOCH2CH2CH3
steps: E is an ester (from parts (ii) and (iii)) of formula C5H10O2; the total relative peak area 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 = 10 matches 10 H
A, 4.02 ppm, triplet, 2H: the OCH2, next to CH2 (2 neighbours + 1 = triplet) and deshielded by O
B, 2.05 ppm, singlet, 3H: CH3 attached to C=O with no H on the neighbouring carbon
C, 1.65 ppm, sextet, 2H: the middle CH2, which has 5 neighbouring H (OCH2 and CH3)
D, 0.95 ppm, triplet, 3H: the terminal CH3, next to a CH2

questions.question: What is the number of chiral centres in a molecule of menthol? Options: A 1, B 2, C 3, D 4.
questions.answer: C (3 chiral centres)
steps: A chiral centre is a carbon bonded to four different groups
Menthol has three ring carbons, each bonded to four different groups (CHOH, CH-CH3, and CH-isopropyl)
So there are 3 chiral centres

keywords: labelled carbons P Q R S
questions.question: Which labelled carbon atom (P, Q, R or S) of menthol is responsible for the 13C NMR peak at 72 ppm? Options: A P, B Q, C R, D S.
questions.answer: B: Q
steps: In 13C NMR a carbon bonded to an oxygen atom (C-OH, alcohol) appears at about 50-90 ppm, here 72 ppm, whereas other alkane-type carbons are below about 50 ppm
In the structure, the OH is attached to carbon Q
So the peak at 72 ppm is due to Q (option B)

questions.question: Four groups warmed menthol with sodium dichromate(VI) in acid and tested the product. Which group recorded the expected results (A One, B Two, C Three, D Four)?
questions.answer: B: Group Two (2,4-DNPH positive, Fehling's negative, PCl5 negative)
steps: Menthol is a secondary alcohol, so warming with acidified dichromate(VI) oxidises it to a ketone (menthone)
A ketone gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH (tick), does not reduce Fehling's solution (cross) and has no -OH, so it gives no misty fumes with PCl5 (cross)
Group Two is the only row with tick, cross, cross, so option B

questions.question: The high-resolution mass spectrum of compound X has a molecular ion peak at m/z = 44.0632. Which compound with Mr 44 gives this peak? (The options are in a diagram shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: C: propane, C3H8
steps: Ethanal and ethenol (both C2H4O) = 24.0000 + 4.0316 + 15.9949 = 44.0265, and CO2 = 12.0000 + 31.9898 = 43.9898, so neither matches
Only C3H8 gives 44.0632, so option C

questions.question: The standard enthalpy change of solution of NH4NO3 is +25.7 kJ mol-1. Calculate the standard entropy change of the surroundings when it dissolves in water at 298 K, with sign and units.
steps: Dissolving is endothermic, so the surroundings lose heat: delta H(system) = +25.7 kJ mol-1 = +25 700 J mol-1
delta S(surroundings) = -delta H(system) / T
delta S(surroundings) = -25 700 / 298 = -86.2 J K-1 mol-1

questions.question: Explain what can be deduced from your answer to (a) about the sign and value of the entropy change of the system when NH4NO3 dissolves.
questions.answer: delta S(system) must be positive and greater than 86.2 J K-1 mol-1, so that delta S(total) is positive for a spontaneous process
steps: Dissolving is spontaneous, so delta S(total) = delta S(system) + delta S(surroundings) must be positive
delta S(surroundings) = -86.2 J K-1 mol-1 (negative), so delta S(system) must be greater than +86.2 J K-1 mol-1
The system entropy increases because ions are released into solution and become more disordered

questions.question: Give a reason why the oxygen used in the combustion of compound X must be dry.
questions.answer: Water vapour in the oxygen would add to the mass of water measured, so the H content would be overestimated
steps: The mass of water produced is used to find the mass of hydrogen in X
Any water already present in the oxygen would be weighed as product water
This would give an incorrect (too high) mass of hydrogen and so a wrong formula

questions.question: A 2.50 g sample of X gives 4.31 g CO2 and 1.32 g H2O on complete combustion. Show that the empirical formula of X is C4H6O3.
questions.answer: Empirical formula C4H6O3
steps: Divide by smallest (0.0735): C : H : O = 1.33 : 1.99 : 1; multiply by 3 gives 4 : 6 : 3
Empirical formula = C4H6O3

questions.question: X gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH, no reaction with Tollens' reagent, effervesces with NaHCO3 (gas turns limewater cloudy), and its 13C NMR has four peaks. Deduce the two possible structures of X and show how the information supports them.
questions.answer: CH3COCH2COOH (3-oxobutanoic acid) or CH3CH2COCOOH (2-oxobutanoic acid)
steps: Orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH shows a C=O group (aldehyde or ketone)
No reaction with Tollens' reagent rules out an aldehyde, so the C=O is a ketone
Effervescence with NaHCO3 giving CO2 (limewater turns cloudy) shows a -COOH group
C4H6O3 has two C=O groups (double bond equivalents = 2), so it must be a keto acid
Possible keto acids with four distinct carbons: CH3COCH2COOH and CH3CH2COCOOH
Each has 4 environments and no symmetry, so both give four 13C peaks

questions.question: Give a chemical test to distinguish between the two compounds from (b)(i), including the reagents and the result for each compound.
questions.answer: Warm with iodine in alkaline solution: CH3COCH2COOH gives a yellow precipitate (CHI3); CH3CH2COCOOH gives no precipitate
steps: Reagents: iodine (I2) dissolved in aqueous NaOH, warmed
CH3COCH2COOH contains a CH3CO- group, so it gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform, CHI3
CH3CH2COCOOH has a CH3CH2CO- group, not CH3CO-, so it gives no yellow precipitate

questions.question: Explain how the number of peaks, their relative peak areas, their chemical shifts and their splitting patterns in the 1H NMR spectrum of X can confirm its structure.
questions.answer: The spectrum has 3 peaks of relative heights 1 : 2 : 3, at about 11, 2.6 and 1.9 ppm, all singlets, which fits CH3COCH2COOH (3-oxobutanoic acid) and not CH3CH2COCOOH
steps: Number of peaks: three peaks means three different hydrogen environments, which matches CH3COCH2COOH (CH3, CH2 and COOH)
Relative heights 1 : 2 : 3 give the ratio of hydrogens: 1 H (COOH), 2 H (CH2) and 3 H (CH3), total 6 H as in C4H6O3

Chemical shifts: about 11 ppm is the acid O-H of COOH (range about 10-12 ppm); about 2.6 ppm is the CH2 next to a C=O; about 1.9-2.2 ppm is the CH3 attached to C=O (data booklet range about 2.1-2.7 ppm)
Splitting: every peak is a singlet because no hydrogens are on adjacent carbons (the CH2 and CH3 are separated by the C=O), as in CH3COCH2COOH
The other isomer, CH3CH2COCOOH, would show a quartet (CH2) and a triplet (CH3), so it is ruled out

questions.question: A high-resolution mass spectrum of compound X has a molecular ion at m/z = 58.0417 and another peak at m/z = 29.0390. Which compound is X? Options: A CH3COCH3, B CH3CH2CHO, C CH3CH2CH2CH3, D CH3CH(CH3)CH3.
questions.answer: B (CH3CH2CHO, propanal)
steps: C3H6O: 3 x 12.0000 + 6 x 1.0078 + 15.9949 = 58.0417, which matches the molecular ion for propanone or propanal
Propanal (CH3CH2CHO) loses CHO to give the C2H5+ ion at m/z 29
Propanone gives CH3CO+ (m/z 43) instead, so the answer is propanal

questions.question: A diagram of a thin-layer chromatogram of substance Y is shown. What is its Rf value? Options: A 0.25, B 0.60, C 0.75, D 1.33.
steps: Rf = distance moved by the substance / distance moved by the solvent front, both measured from the baseline
Measuring on the diagram: baseline to solvent front is about 240 units and baseline to the spot is about 178 units (spot about three quarters of the way up)
Rf = 178 / 240 = 0.74, which is closest to 0.75, so option C (Rf cannot exceed 1, so D is impossible)

questions.question: Molecule A reacts in an intramolecular reaction with an acid catalyst to form cyclic ester B. Draw the structure of B.
questions.answer: Cyclic ester B (a lactone): a five-membered ring containing -O-C(=O)-CH2-CH2-CH(CH3)-, i.e. 5-methyloxolan-2-one (4-pentanolide), C5H8O2
steps: Molecule A is 4-hydroxypentanoic acid, CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2COOH, with an -OH and a -COOH in the same molecule
Intramolecular esterification: the -OH on carbon 4 attacks the COOH carbon and water is lost, forming an ester link inside the molecule
The ring contains the ester C(=O) carbon, two CH2 groups, the CH(CH3) carbon and the ring oxygen: five atoms in total

questions.question: Draw the condensation polymer C formed from A by intermolecular reaction, showing two repeat units.
questions.answer: -[O-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)]-n drawn as two units: -O-CH(CH3)CH2CH2C(=O)-O-CH(CH3)CH2CH2C(=O)- with the open bonds at both ends shown
steps: Intermolecular reaction: the -OH of one molecule of A reacts with the -COOH of another, giving an ester link and losing water each time
A has both groups, so a polyester forms by condensation polymerisation
Repeat unit: -O-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-; show two such units joined through an ester -C(=O)-O- link, with continuation bonds at each end

questions.question: Explain why the entropy change of the system is greater for Reaction 1 (intramolecular, forming cyclic ester B) than for Reaction 2 (intermolecular, forming polymer C).
questions.answer: Reaction 1 turns one molecule into two (B and water), increasing the number of molecules; Reaction 2 joins molecules together, so the number of molecules changes much less
steps: Reaction 1: one molecule of A gives one molecule of B plus one molecule of water, so the number of particles increases from 1 to 2
Reaction 2: many molecules of A join into one long polymer chain with water released, so the number of separate molecules hardly increases
A greater increase in the number of molecules (more disorder) gives a larger entropy change, so Reaction 1 has the greater delta S(system)

questions.question: Give the molecular formula of the triester shown in the question.
questions.answer: C9H14O6
steps: The triester is propane-1,2,3-triyl triethanoate (glyceryl triethanoate): a C3H5 backbone with three -OCOCH3 groups
Molecular formula C9H14O6

questions.question: Complete the equation for the alkaline hydrolysis of the triester with excess aqueous NaOH, showing the structures of the products.
questions.answer: C9H14O6 + 3NaOH -> 3CH3COONa + CH2(OH)CH(OH)CH2OH (sodium ethanoate and propane-1,2,3-triol)
steps: Alkaline hydrolysis breaks each ester link: three C(=O)-O bonds are broken
With excess NaOH the acid part is formed as its sodium salt, three CH3COO-Na+ (sodium ethanoate)
The alcohol part is the triol, propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol), HOCH2CH(OH)CH2OH
Three NaOH are needed per triester, so the balancing number in front of NaOH is 3

questions.question: Identify Reagent P in the reactions of ethanoyl chloride, CH3COCl, shown in the scheme.
questions.answer: Water, H2O
steps: The acyl chloride CH3COCl is converted to the carboxylic acid CH3COOH
The Cl is replaced by OH, which is the effect of reacting with water (hydrolysis), releasing HCl

questions.question: Write a balanced equation for Reaction Q in the ethanoyl chloride scheme (state symbols not required).
questions.answer: CH3COCl + 2NH3 -> CH3CONH2 + NH4Cl
steps: Reaction Q converts CH3COCl to the primary amide ethanamide, so the reagent is ammonia (concentrated or excess)
One NH3 substitutes for Cl, and a second NH3 takes up the HCl produced to form NH4Cl
Balanced: CH3COCl + 2NH3 -> CH3CONH2 + NH4Cl (CH3COCl + NH3 -> CH3CONH2 + HCl is also accepted)

questions.question: Suggest the structural formula of Reagent R in the ethanoyl chloride scheme.
questions.answer: CH3SH (methanethiol)
steps: The product is CH3C(=O)-S-CH3, in which the Cl of the acyl chloride has been replaced by -SCH3
The reagent supplying this group is the thiol CH3SH, with loss of HCl

questions.question: Draw the skeletal formula of Reagent S in the ethanoyl chloride scheme.
questions.answer: N-methylethanamine, CH3CH2NHCH3: a skeletal zigzag chain of N with one methyl and one ethyl group (and an H on N)
steps: The product is CH3C(=O)N(CH3)CH2CH3, a tertiary amide, so the N has gained a methyl and an ethyl group
The reagent is therefore the secondary amine CH3CH2-NH-CH3, which replaces Cl with the N (HCl lost)
Skeletal formula: ethyl group (two-segment zigzag) bonded to NH, which is bonded to a methyl line

questions.question: Sodium ethanoate reacts with 2-methylpropanoyl chloride to form compound Z and NaCl. Z has a molecular ion at m/z 130, IR peaks at 1820 and 1754 cm-1, and five 13C NMR peaks. Deduce the structure of Z.
questions.answer: Z = CH3COOCOCH(CH3)2 (ethanoic 2-methylpropanoic anhydride, C6H10O3)
steps: Sodium ethanoate and an acyl chloride give an acid anhydride with NaCl as by-product
The mixed anhydride from CH3COO- and (CH3)2CHCOCl is CH3COOCOCH(CH3)2
Its formula is C6H10O3: M = 6 x 12.01 + 10 x 1.008 + 3 x 16.00 = 130.1, matching m/z 130
Two C=O bands at 1820 and 1754 cm-1 are typical of an acid anhydride
Five 13C environments: acetyl CH3, acetyl C=O, isobutyryl C=O, CH, and the two equivalent CH3 groups
1H NMR would show a 3H singlet (CH3CO), a 1H septet (CH) and a 6H doublet (2 x CH3)

questions.question: How many peaks are there in the low-resolution 1H NMR spectrum of 2-methylpropan-2-ol? Options: A one, B two, C three, D four.
questions.answer: B (two)
steps: 2-methylpropan-2-ol is (CH3)3COH
There are two proton environments: the 9 equivalent CH3 protons and the OH proton
So the low-resolution spectrum has two peaks

questions.question: Which compound has three peaks with relative peak areas 3:2:1 in its low-resolution 1H NMR spectrum? Options: A propanal, B propane, C propan-1-ol, D propan-2-ol.
questions.answer: A (propanal, CH3CH2CHO)
steps: Propanal has CH3 (3H), CH2 (2H) and CHO (1H): three environments
Their peak areas are 3:2:1
Propane has two environments (6:2), propan-1-ol has four (3:2:2:1), and propan-2-ol has 6:1:1

questions.question: Which compound does not have a singlet peak in its high-resolution 1H NMR spectrum? Options: A butanoic acid, B butanone, C butanal, D butan-1-ol.
questions.answer: C (butanal)
steps: Butanoic acid has a COOH singlet
Butanone has a CH3CO singlet (CH3 next to C=O has no H neighbours)
Butan-1-ol has an OH singlet (exchangeable proton)
Butanal, CH3CH2CH2CHO, has a CHO proton coupled to CH2 (a triplet), so no singlet

questions.topic: Mobile and Stationary Phases in HPLC
questions.question: In HPLC, the mobile and stationary phases are... (Options A-D are shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: D: mobile phase liquid, stationary phase solid
steps: In HPLC the mobile phase is a liquid solvent pumped under high pressure through the column
The stationary phase is a solid (e.g. silica packed in the column, often with a bonded layer), so liquid mobile and solid stationary: option D
Gas as the mobile phase belongs to gas chromatography

questions.question: Write the equation for the acid dissociation constant, Ka, of hexanoic acid, C5H11COOH.
questions.answer: Ka = [H+][C5H11COO-] / [C5H11COOH]
steps: C5H11COOH <=> H+ + C5H11COO-
Ka = [H+][C5H11COO-] / [C5H11COOH]

questions.question: Calculate the pH of a 0.100 mol dm-3 solution of hexanoic acid, given pKa = 4.88.
steps: Weak acid, so [H+] = sqrt(Ka x c) = sqrt(1.32 x 10^-5 x 0.100) = 1.15 x 10^-3 mol dm-3

questions.question: Hexanoic acid has solubility 1.08 g per 100 g water and butyl ethanoate (its isomer) has solubility 0.68 g per 100 g water. Explain the difference in terms of hydrogen bonding with water.
questions.answer: Hexanoic acid can donate and accept hydrogen bonds with water (via its O-H and C=O), while butyl ethanoate can only accept them (via C=O), so hexanoic acid dissolves more
steps: Hexanoic acid has an O-H group, so it can form hydrogen bonds with water as a donor
Both molecules have a C=O group, which can accept hydrogen bonds from water
Butyl ethanoate has no O-H group, so it forms fewer hydrogen bonds with water
Stronger hydrogen bonding with water makes hexanoic acid more soluble

questions.question: 10 g of compound A contains 6.21 g carbon and 1.03 g hydrogen, the rest oxygen. Calculate its empirical formula, showing all working.
questions.answer: C3H6O
steps: Divide by smallest (0.173): C = 3.00; H = 5.92; O = 1.00
Empirical formula = C3H6O

questions.question: State how you might use the empirical formula from (b)(i) and a mass spectrum of compound A to prove that A is an isomer of hexanoic acid.
questions.answer: Empirical formula C3H6O has Mr 58; the molecular ion at m/z 116 gives C6H12O2 (2 x C3H6O), the same formula as hexanoic acid
steps: Empirical formula mass C3H6O = 58
A molecular ion peak at m/z 116 gives n = 116/58 = 2, so the molecular formula is C6H12O2
C6H12O2 is the molecular formula of hexanoic acid, so A is an isomer

questions.question: A series of tests was performed on compound A (C6H12O2). Deduce the structure of A and justify it using all the test results.
questions.answer: A is a hydroxy-ketone with a tertiary -OH and a chiral centre, e.g. 3-hydroxy-3-methylpentan-2-one, CH3COC(OH)(CH3)CH2CH3
steps: Test 1: misty fumes with PCl5 means A contains an -OH group (alcohol or carboxylic acid)
Test 2: orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH means a C=O group (aldehyde or ketone); C6H12O2 has only one degree of unsaturation, which this C=O uses, so A is not also an acid or ester
Test 3: no reaction with Benedict's/Fehling's, so the C=O is a ketone, not an aldehyde
Test 4: acidified dichromate stays orange, so the OH is not on a primary or secondary carbon: it is a tertiary alcohol
Test 5: A rotates plane-polarised light, so it has a chiral centre (a carbon with four different groups): here the C bearing OH, CH3, C2H5 and COCH3
Structure fitting everything with six carbons: CH3-CO-C(OH)(CH3)-CH2CH3

questions.question: Compound B (C6H12O2) contains a ring of six carbon atoms and its 13C NMR spectrum has only two peaks, one at 69 ppm. Draw the structure of B.
questions.answer: Cyclohexane-1,4-diol (a six-membered carbon ring with OH groups on carbons 1 and 4)
steps: The ring of six carbons with two O atoms and no C=O gives C6H12O2 as two OH groups on the ring
Only two 13C peaks means a symmetrical molecule: C1 and C4 equivalent, C2, C3, C5 and C6 equivalent
A peak at 69 ppm is typical of a C-O carbon (CH-OH)
So B is cyclohexane-1,4-diol

questions.question: HPLC uses a non-polar stationary phase and a methanol/water mobile phase. A mixture of octane, octanal and octan-1-ol is injected. What is the order of retention times?
questions.answer: Shortest to longest: octan-1-ol, octanal, octane
steps: The stationary phase is non-polar, so polar compounds are carried through more quickly by the polar mobile phase
Octan-1-ol is the most polar (O-H, hydrogen bonding) and elutes first
Octanal has a polar C=O but no O-H, so it elutes next
Octane is non-polar and is retained most strongly, so it elutes last

questions.question: In gas chromatography, a gas containing a mixture is passed over a liquid stationary phase. The main reason a mixture is separated into components is that they have different... Options: A boiling temperatures, B forces of attraction to the liquid, C relative molecular masses, D volatilities.
questions.answer: B (forces of attraction to the liquid)
steps: In GC the components partition between the gas and the liquid stationary phase
Each component has different intermolecular attractions to the liquid stationary phase
Components with weaker attractions spend more time in the gas and emerge first, so they separate

questions.question: Which change decreases the retention time in gas chromatography? Options: A decreasing the column temperature, B increasing the carrier gas flow rate, C decreasing the amount of sample, D increasing the column length.
questions.answer: B (increasing the carrier gas flow rate)
steps: Retention time depends on how long a component stays on the stationary phase
Increasing the carrier gas flow rate moves the components through the column faster
Lower temperature, longer column and more sample all increase retention time

questions.question: Three straight-chain carbonyl isomers A, B and C have formula C5H10O. Only A reacts with Tollens' reagent; only B reacts with iodine in alkali to give pale yellow crystals. Draw the three structures.
questions.answer: A = CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO (pentanal); B = CH3COCH2CH2CH3 (pentan-2-one); C = CH3CH2COCH2CH3 (pentan-3-one)
steps: Tollens' silver mirror shows an aldehyde, so A is pentanal
Iodine in alkali giving a yellow precipitate shows a CH3CO group, so B is pentan-2-one
C is the remaining straight-chain ketone with no CH3CO group and no aldehyde, so it is pentan-3-one

questions.question: Give the IUPAC name for CH3CH2CH(OH)CN, the product of propanal with HCN.
questions.answer: 2-hydroxybutanenitrile
steps: The CN carbon is C1 of the chain (nitrile)
The CH(OH) carbon is C2
The chain has four carbons: CN, CH(OH), CH2, CH3, so the name is 2-hydroxybutanenitrile

questions.question: Describe how you could distinguish between pure samples of the two optical isomers of 2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
questions.answer: Measure the rotation of plane-polarised light in a polarimeter: each enantiomer rotates it by the same amount in opposite directions
steps: Pass plane-polarised light through a sample in a polarimeter
Each pure enantiomer rotates the plane of polarisation by the same angle
The two enantiomers rotate it in opposite directions (one clockwise, one anticlockwise)

questions.question: Explain, with reference to the mechanism, why the reaction of propanal with HCN produces a racemic mixture.
questions.answer: The C=O carbon is planar, so CN- attacks from above and below with equal probability, giving equal amounts of the two enantiomers
steps: The carbonyl carbon in propanal is sp2 and planar
CN- can attack from either face of the planar C=O with equal probability
Each attack gives one enantiomer, so equal amounts of both are formed
Equal amounts of the two enantiomers form a racemic mixture (no net optical activity)

questions.question: Propanone, an isomer of propanal, reacts with HCN in the presence of KCN. Draw the skeletal formula of the product.
questions.answer: (CH3)2C(OH)CN, 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanenitrile
steps: CN- attacks the C=O carbon of propanone (CH3COCH3)
The alkoxide is protonated by HCN
Product: (CH3)2C(OH)CN

questions.question: State why the product from (c)(i) does not show optical isomerism.
questions.answer: The central carbon has two identical CH3 groups, so it is not a chiral centre
steps: A chiral centre needs four different groups on one carbon
In (CH3)2C(OH)CN, the central carbon has two identical CH3 groups
So the molecule is achiral and has no optical isomers

questions.question: Identify the chemical shift range and carbon environment of one peak expected in the 13C NMR spectra of both propanal and propanone.
questions.answer: About 190-220 ppm, the C=O (carbonyl) carbon
steps: Both propanal and propanone contain a C=O group
The carbonyl carbon is strongly deshielded by the O atom
Its 13C chemical shift is in the range 190-220 ppm

questions.question: State the number of peaks you would expect in the 13C NMR spectrum of propanal and of propanone.
questions.answer: Propanal: 3 peaks; propanone: 2 peaks
steps: Propanal CH3CH2CHO has three different carbons
Propanone CH3COCH3 has two environments: the two equivalent CH3 groups and the C=O carbon

questions.question: Sketch the low-resolution 1H NMR spectrum of Tris, C4H11NO3, using the Data Booklet.
questions.answer: Three singlets with relative areas 6:3:2: CH2 (6H), OH (3H) and NH2 (2H)
steps: Tris is (HOCH2)3C-NH2, with a central quaternary C
The three CH2 groups are equivalent: 6H, on a peak around 3.5-4 ppm
The three OH protons (3H) and the NH2 protons (2H) are each a singlet (no adjacent C-H), with broad peaks typical of exchangeable protons
Sketch: peaks in the ratio 6:3:2 from left to right by chemical shift

questions.question: Explain how a mixture of Tris and its conjugate acid acts as a buffer when a small amount of acid is added.
questions.answer: Added H+ is removed by Tris (the base), forming more conjugate acid, so the pH changes only slightly
steps: Tris is a Bronsted-Lowry base and its conjugate acid is TrisH+
When a small amount of H+ is added, it reacts with Tris: Tris + H+ -> TrisH+
The equilibrium TrisH+ <=> Tris + H+ shifts to the left, so the [H+] rises only a little
The added acid is mopped up, so the pH stays nearly constant

questions.question: Write the expression for the Ka of the conjugate acid of Tris.
questions.answer: Ka = [H+][Tris] / [TrisH+]
steps: TrisH+ <=> Tris + H+
Ka = [H+][Tris] / [TrisH+]

questions.question: 100 g of the solid acid salt (Tris.HCl, Mr about 157.6) is mixed with 500 cm3 of 0.200 mol dm-3 Tris, with no change in volume. Ka of the conjugate acid is 8.413 x 10^-9 mol dm-3. Calculate the pH of the buffer.
steps: Acid salt is TrisH+Cl- with Mr = 157.6, so moles = 100 / 157.6 = 0.634 mol, giving [TrisH+] = 0.634 / 0.500 = 1.27 mol dm-3
Moles of Tris = 0.200 x 0.500 = 0.100 mol, giving [Tris] = 0.200 mol dm-3

questions.question: 0.0150 g of chloroethanoic acid (Mr 94.5) is dissolved in 1500 cm3 of water and the pH is 3.42. Calculate the Ka of chloroethanoic acid.
questions.answer: Ka = 1.37 x 10^-3 mol dm-3 (about 1.4 x 10^-3 mol dm-3)
steps: [H+] = 10^-3.42 = 3.80 x 10^-4 mol dm-3, and [ClCH2COO-] = [H+] because the acid dissociates 1:1 (water's H+ ignored)

Ka = 1.37 x 10^-3 mol dm-3. Note: the [H+] from the pH is larger than the stated acid concentration, so the data are not self-consistent; the intended working takes [HA] as the stated concentration (the acid is only slightly dissociated assumption)

questions.question: Explain how the titration curve of Tris with chloroethanoic acid shows that Tris and its conjugate acid act as a buffer.
questions.answer: Between about 2 and 16 cm3 of acid, the pH stays almost constant (about 8.5), so the Tris / conjugate acid mixture resists pH change when acid is added
steps: On the graph the pH falls only from about 8.9 to about 8.4 over the first 16 cm3 of acid, a long nearly flat region
In this region Tris (a base) and its conjugate acid are both present in appreciable amounts: added H+ is removed by Tris, which forms more conjugate acid, so [H+] and pH hardly change
The sharp fall at 20 cm3 occurs only when the Tris has been used up (equivalence), so the buffer has run out

questions.question: Use the graph to estimate the pH of the salt formed when Tris is neutralised with chloroethanoic acid.
questions.answer: About pH 6 (read at the midpoint of the vertical section at 20 cm3, between about pH 7 and pH 5)
steps: The salt forms at the equivalence point, where 20 cm3 of acid has been added
The vertical section of the curve at 20 cm3 runs from about pH 7.2 to about pH 4.8; its midpoint gives the pH of the salt solution, about 6
The salt of a weak base with an acid is slightly acidic, consistent with a pH below 7

questions.question: Suggest a reason why buffers are so important in biological systems.
questions.answer: They keep pH nearly constant, so enzymes and proteins keep their shape and activity
steps: Enzymes and proteins work only within a narrow pH range
Buffers resist pH changes from acids or bases produced in metabolism
A stable pH keeps biological reactions working efficiently

questions.question: The chromatogram of substance X is shown. What is its Rf value? Options: A 0.28, B 0.62, C 0.70, D 0.86.
steps: Rf = distance from baseline to spot / distance from baseline to solvent front
Measured on the diagram: spot about 198 units above the baseline; solvent front about 282 units above the baseline
Rf = 198 / 282 = 0.70, so option C

questions.question: Explain why lactic acid formed in muscles is optically active while lactic acid made by the laboratory synthesis from ethanal is not. Define any terms used.
questions.answer: Muscle lactic acid is one enantiomer, made enzymatically (optically active); the laboratory route attacks a planar carbonyl from both sides and gives a racemic mixture (not optically active)
steps: Optical activity: rotation of plane-polarised light by a sample of chiral molecules; a chiral centre is a C with four different groups
Muscle lactic acid is made by a stereospecific enzyme, so only one enantiomer forms
A single enantiomer rotates plane-polarised light, so it is optically active
Laboratory synthesis: ethanal + HCN gives CN- attacking the planar C=O from either side with equal probability
Equal amounts of both enantiomers form a racemic mixture, which is optically inactive because the rotations cancel

questions.question: Draw the structure of a section of poly(lactic acid), PLA, showing two repeat units.
questions.answer: -[O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)]n- ; two units: -O-CH(CH3)-CO-O-CH(CH3)-CO-
steps: Lactic acid is CH3CH(OH)COOH and forms a polyester by ester links
Each repeat unit is -O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-
Two repeat units are joined by ester links: -O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-

questions.question: Compound X has empirical formula C3H4O2 and molar mass 144 g mol-1. Determine its molecular formula.
questions.answer: C6H8O4
steps: Empirical formula mass C3H4O2 = 3 x 12 + 4 x 1 + 2 x 16 = 72
Molecular formula = C6H8O4

questions.question: A simplified high-resolution 1H NMR spectrum of X is shown. State what the number of peaks, their relative peak areas and splitting patterns show about the structure of X.
questions.answer: Two peaks: two hydrogen environments, in the ratio 1 : 3, with the 1H quartet and 3H doublet showing a CH(CH3) unit
steps: Number of peaks: two, so X has only two different hydrogen environments (a CH and a CH3), which means the molecule is symmetrical
Relative peak areas 1 : 3 show one H and three H in the two environments: a CH and a CH3, repeated twice to give 8 H in C6H8O4
Splitting: the 1H peak (about 5 ppm) is a quartet, so its carbon is next to a CH3 (3 H, n + 1 = 4); the 3H peak (about 1.3 ppm) is a doublet, so its CH3 is next to a single CH
Together: X contains -CH(CH3)- units with no other hydrogens on neighbouring carbons

questions.question: A simplified 13C NMR spectrum of X is shown. State what additional information about the structure of X it gives.
questions.answer: Three carbon environments (3 peaks): C=O of an ester at about 168 ppm, C-O (CH-O) at about 72 ppm and CH3 at about 15 ppm; X has six carbons so each environment occurs twice (symmetry)
steps: Three peaks means three different carbon environments, so the six carbons in X come in identical pairs and the molecule is symmetrical
The peak at about 168 ppm is a C=O carbon of an ester (data booklet range about 160-185 ppm), which tells us the ester group is present, not shown by the 1H spectrum
The peak at about 72 ppm is a carbon singly bonded to oxygen (C-O, 50-90 ppm) and the peak at about 15 ppm is an alkyl CH3

questions.question: Draw the structure of X using the information from (b)(ii) to (b)(iv).
questions.answer: Lactide (3,6-dimethyl-1,4-dioxane-2,5-dione): a six-membered ring O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-, C6H8O4
steps: X is a cyclic diester made from two lactic acid molecules, each contributing a CH(CH3) and a C(=O)O link; formula C6H8O4 (M = 144)
The ring is O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-, joined back to the first O to close the six-membered ring
This has two equivalent CH(CH3) units (1H quartet, 3H doublet) and three carbon environments (C=O, CH, CH3), as seen in both spectra

questions.question: Which is correct for the labels on the axes of the HPLC chromatogram? (Options not in text.)
questions.answer: D: x-axis = time, y-axis = absorption
steps: An HPLC chromatogram plots the detector response (here absorption) against retention time
The x-axis is therefore time (0 to 15, retention time) and the y-axis is absorption
Rf is a quantity used in thin-layer and paper chromatography, not HPLC, so options B and C are wrong

questions.question: Which is correct for the components E, F and G in the HPLC chromatogram? (Options not in text.)
questions.answer: D: G is most attracted to the stationary phase; F is most abundant
steps: The component most strongly attracted to the stationary phase is held longest, so it has the longest retention time: G (about 7.5 min)
The peak area is proportional to the amount of each component; F has the largest peak, so F is the most abundant
G and F together make option D

questions.question: State the essential condition for using LiAlH4 as a reducing agent.
questions.answer: Anhydrous (dry) conditions, using a dry ether solvent
steps: LiAlH4 reacts violently with water and protic solvents
So the reaction must be carried out in dry ether under anhydrous conditions

questions.question: Complete the mechanism for the reduction of propanone with LiAlH4, showing the intermediate and the final product, including curly arrows, lone pairs and dipoles.
questions.answer: Intermediate: (CH3)2CH-O-AlH3- (alkoxide complex); after acid workup the product is propan-2-ol, (CH3)2CHOH
steps: Hydride H- from AlH4- attacks the delta+ carbon of the C=O group (curly arrow from the Al-H bond to C)
The C=O pi bond breaks, curly arrow onto O, forming an alkoxide intermediate
The intermediate is (CH3)2CH-O-AlH3- with a Li+ counter ion
Adding dilute acid (H+) protonates the alkoxide (curly arrow from O-H+ onto O), giving propan-2-ol

questions.question: Explain why LiAlH4 reduces carbonyl compounds but not alkenes, even though both contain pi bonds.
questions.answer: The C=O bond is polar with an electrophilic delta+ carbon that hydride attacks; the C=C bond is non-polar and electron-rich, so it is not attacked by the nucleophilic hydride
steps: The C=O bond is polar: C is delta+ and O is delta-
The hydride ion (nucleophile) is attracted to the electron-deficient carbonyl carbon
The C=C bond is non-polar and electron-rich, so there is no delta+ carbon for hydride to attack
Hence LiAlH4 reduces carbonyls but not alkenes

questions.question: Complete the table for the three straight-chain structural isomers of C5H11Br. (The table itself is shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: 1-bromopentane (zigzag of 5 C with Br on the end carbon): 5 peaks; 2-bromopentane (Br on carbon 2): 5 peaks; 3-bromopentane (Br on the middle carbon): 3 peaks
steps: The three straight-chain isomers of C5H11Br have Br on carbon 1, 2 or 3 of a five-carbon chain (Br on C4 or C5 repeats C2 or C1)
1-bromopentane, CH2BrCH2CH2CH2CH3: all five carbons are in different environments, so 5 peaks
2-bromopentane, CH3CHBrCH2CH2CH3: no symmetry, so 5 peaks
3-bromopentane, CH3CH2CHBrCH2CH3: symmetrical, so the two CH3 carbons are equivalent and the two CH2 carbons are equivalent, giving 3 peaks

questions.question: The high-resolution 1H NMR spectrum of one of the C5H11Br isomers is shown. Deduce which isomer is present, explaining the splitting patterns and chemical shifts, and give the relative peak areas.
questions.answer: 3-bromopentane, (CH3CH2)2CHBr: peaks at about 4.0 ppm (1H, quintet), 1.9 ppm (4H, quintet) and 1.0 ppm (6H, triplet), relative areas 1 : 4 : 6
steps: The spectrum has three groups of peaks, so three hydrogen environments; this matches 3-bromopentane (1-bromopentane and 2-bromopentane would each give five)

About 4.0 ppm: the single CHBr hydrogen, the highest shift because it is bonded to the carbon carrying Br (data booklet range about 3.1-4.2 ppm); it has 4 neighbouring H on the two CH2 groups, so n + 1 = 5, a quintet; area 1
About 1.9 ppm: the two equivalent CH2 groups (4H); each is next to the CHBr (1 H) and a CH3 (3 H), 4 neighbours, so a quintet; area 4
About 1.0 ppm: the two equivalent CH3 groups (6H), next to a CH2 (2 H), so a triplet (1 : 2 : 1); area 6; this is the lowest shift of all (alkyl CH3, range about 0.7-1.2 ppm)
Relative areas: 1 : 4 : 6, which add to 11 H as in C5H11Br

questions.question: Draw the SN2 mechanism for the reaction of 1-bromopropane with hydroxide ions in aqueous solution, including curly arrows, dipoles and lone pairs.
questions.answer: OH- attacks the delta+ C bonded to Br from the side opposite Br; the C-Br bond breaks as Br- leaves, giving propan-1-ol in a single step via a transition state
steps: The C-Br bond is polar: C is delta+ and Br is delta-
OH- lone pair attacks the delta+ carbon from the side opposite the C-Br bond (curly arrow from lone pair to C)
A transition state forms with partial O-C and C-Br bonds, with the C-Br bond breaking
The C-Br bond breaks with the electron pair going to Br (curly arrow onto Br), giving CH3CH2CH2OH and Br-

questions.question: In GC, which one of the following would increase the retention time for an alcohol? Options: A increasing the flow rate of mobile phase, B increasing the polarity of the stationary phase, C decreasing the polarity of the stationary phase, D increasing the polarity of the mobile phase.
questions.answer: B (increasing the polarity of the stationary phase)
steps: Alcohols are polar and form hydrogen bonds
A more polar stationary phase interacts more strongly with the polar alcohol
The alcohol is retained longer, so its retention time increases

questions.question: Draw the skeletal formula of 3-methylbutyl ethanoate, CH3COOCH2CH2CH(CH3)2.
questions.answer: Skeletal formula: CH3-C(=O)-O-CH2-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH3 (ethanoate ester, C=O and ester O drawn)
steps: Draw the acid part as CH3C(=O)O- (ethanoate)
Attach the O to CH2CH2CH(CH3)2 (3-methylbutyl)
Show the C=O as a double bond and the ester O as a single bond

questions.question: Use the IR spectrum of 3-methylbutyl ethanoate to identify one peak resulting from a bond in the ester group, giving the bond and its wavenumber range.
questions.answer: C=O stretch in the ester group at about 1735-1750 cm-1 (strong peak)
steps: The ester group contains a C=O bond
The C=O stretch of an ester absorbs strongly at 1735-1750 cm-1
This strong peak is seen in the spectrum

questions.question: Show that the IR spectrum of 3-methylbutyl ethanoate confirms there is no alcohol remaining in the sample.
questions.answer: There is no broad absorption between 3200 and 3550 cm-1 (the O-H stretch of an alcohol); the transmittance stays near 90-95% in that region
steps: An alcohol would show a broad, strong O-H stretching absorption at about 3200-3550 cm-1 (3230-3550 for alcohols in the data booklet)
In the spectrum the trace is almost flat in this region, with no broad trough, so no alcohol O-H is present
The only strong peaks are the C-H stretch near 2900-3000 cm-1, the ester C=O near 1740 cm-1 and C-O near 1240 cm-1, all consistent with the pure ester

questions.question: Show that the structure of ethyl ethanoate, CH3COOCH2CH3, is consistent with its high-resolution 1H NMR spectrum, using all the data in the spectrum (peak areas and splitting patterns).
questions.answer: Three peaks with areas 650 : 975 : 975 (2 : 3 : 3), at about 4.1 ppm (quartet), 2.0 ppm (singlet) and 1.2 ppm (triplet): consistent with OCH2, CH3CO and CH2CH3 in CH3COOCH2CH3
steps: Number of peaks: three, so three hydrogen environments, as in CH3COOCH2CH3 (CH3-C=O, OCH2, and CH3 of ethyl)
Relative areas 650 : 975 : 975 simplify to 2 : 3 : 3, giving the number of H in each environment: 2H (OCH2) and 3H, 3H (the two CH3 groups), total 8 H as in C4H8O2
Peak at about 4.1 ppm (area 2): OCH2, deshielded by the oxygen; it is a quartet because there are 3 H on the neighbouring CH3 (n + 1 = 4)
Peak at about 1.2 ppm (area 3): CH3 of the ethyl group, a triplet because 2 H on the neighbouring CH2 (n + 1 = 3)
Peak at about 2.0 ppm (area 3): CH3 attached to the C=O, a singlet because the carbonyl carbon has no H, so there is no splitting

questions.question: Ethyl ethanoate has three other ester isomers. Draw their structures.
questions.answer: Methyl propanoate, CH3CH2COOCH3; propyl methanoate, HCOOCH2CH2CH3; 1-methylethyl methanoate, HCOOCH(CH3)2
steps: Esters of formula C4H8O2 are RCOOR' with R + R' totalling C3 plus the ester C atoms
Swap the acid and alcohol parts: ethanoate with ethyl gives propanoate with methyl
Methanoate (HCOO-) with propyl or isopropyl gives the other two esters

questions.question: Explain to what extent the three isomers of ethyl ethanoate can be distinguished using 13C NMR spectroscopy.
questions.answer: Partly: 1-methylethyl methanoate has 3 peaks (two equivalent CH3), so it can be identified, but methyl propanoate and propyl methanoate each give 4 peaks and cannot be distinguished by peak number alone
steps: Ethyl ethanoate, methyl propanoate and propyl methanoate each have 4 different carbon environments
1-methylethyl methanoate, HCOOCH(CH3)2, has 2 equivalent CH3 carbons, giving only 3 peaks
So 1-methylethyl methanoate can be distinguished by its 3 peaks
Methyl propanoate and propyl methanoate both give 4 peaks, so 13C NMR cannot fully separate them

questions.question: Carvone shows: A geometric and optical isomerism, B geometric isomerism only, C optical isomerism only, D neither.
questions.answer: C (optical isomerism only)
steps: Carvone has a chiral carbon (C5 in the ring bearing the isopropenyl group), so it shows optical isomerism
The ring C=C cannot show E/Z (geometric) isomerism because one C has two identical ring-linked arrangements
So carvone shows optical isomerism only

questions.question: Which reagent gives a positive result with carvone? Options: A Tollens' reagent, B aqueous sodium carbonate, C iodine in alkali, D 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine.
questions.answer: D (2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine)
steps: Carvone is a ketone (C=O), so it gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH
Tollens' reagent needs an aldehyde, so it is negative
Sodium carbonate tests for COOH, which carvone lacks
Iodine in alkali needs a CH3CO group, which carvone does not have

questions.question: How many peaks would be expected in the 13C NMR spectrum of carvone? Options: A 10, B 9, C 8, D 7.
steps: Carvone is C10H14O with 10 carbon atoms
It has no symmetry, so every carbon is in a different environment
So 10 peaks are expected

questions.question: Deduce the name of the alcohol used to make ester X (C8H16O2) by reaction with ethanoyl chloride.
questions.answer: 3-methylpentan-3-ol, (CH3CH2)2C(OH)CH3
steps: X is an ester CH3C(=O)-O-R; the acyl part (from ethanoyl chloride) is CH3CO-, so the alcohol part is R-OH
R is the carbon bonded to the ester O, which carries one CH3 and two CH2CH3 groups
The alcohol is (CH3CH2)2C(OH)CH3, a tertiary alcohol: a pentane chain with OH and CH3 both on carbon 3, so 3-methylpentan-3-ol (R-OH + CH3COCl -> ester + HCl)

questions.question: Complete the labelling of the structure of X to show each of the other proton environments, clearly linking any that are the same.
questions.answer: Three more labels: b on the CH3 of the CH3C(=O) group; c on both CH2 groups (linked as the same environment); d on both CH3 of the ethyl groups (linked as the same environment)
steps: a (given) is the CH3 on the central carbon
b: the CH3 attached to the ester C=O, a separate environment
c: the two CH2 groups are equivalent (both bonded to the same quaternary carbon and to a CH3), so they share one label, linked by a line
d: the two CH3 groups of the ethyl chains are equivalent, so they share one label; this gives four hydrogen environments in total (a, b, c, d)

questions.question: Describe three ways the high-resolution 1H NMR spectrum can be used to distinguish between the methyl groups in X, other than peak a.
questions.answer: Chemical shift, splitting pattern (n+1 rule) and relative peak area (number of H) differ for each methyl group
steps: Chemical shift: CH3 groups in different environments (e.g. next to C=O or O) appear at different ppm
Splitting pattern: a CH3 next to a CH2 gives a triplet, a CH3 next to a CH gives a doublet, and a CH3 with no neighbours gives a singlet
Peak area: the integration (relative area) shows how many H are in each environment

questions.topic: Carboxylic Acid Isomer with Five Carbon Peaks
questions.question: Draw a possible skeletal structure for a carboxylic acid isomer of X (C8H16O2) that has five peaks in its 13C NMR spectrum.
questions.answer: 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutanoic acid, (CH3)3C-C(CH3)2-COOH
steps: Carboxylic acid isomer needs a COOH group and C8H16O2
(CH3)3C-C(CH3)2-COOH has 8 carbons and 16 H
Carbon environments: COOH, quaternary C next to COOH, its two CH3 groups (1 peak), the tert-butyl quaternary C and its three CH3 groups (1 peak): 5 peaks in total

questions.question: Add a single curly arrow to Step 1 and a single curly arrow to Step 2 in the aspirin mechanism.
questions.answer: Step 1: a curly arrow from a lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen of the anhydride to the H+; Step 2: a curly arrow from a lone pair on the phenol oxygen of 2-hydroxybenzoic acid to the delta+ carbon of the protonated C=OH+ group
steps: Step 1 is protonation: the lone pair on the C=O oxygen attacks H+ (arrow starts on the lone pair on the O and ends at H+), giving the C=OH+ group
Step 2 is nucleophilic attack: the lone pair on the phenol O-H oxygen attacks the electron-poor carbon, which is more positive after protonation
The arrow starts on the lone pair of the phenol oxygen and points to the carbonyl carbon (the arrow on the C=OH+ group moving electrons onto oxygen is already drawn)

questions.topic: Role of H+ in Aspirin Synthesis
questions.question: State the role of the H+ ion in the synthesis of aspirin.
questions.answer: H+ acts as a catalyst: it protonates the anhydride C=O, making the carbon more electrophilic so the phenol attacks more readily
steps: H+ protonates the C=O oxygen of ethanoic anhydride
This increases the delta+ on the carbonyl carbon
The OH group of 2-hydroxybenzoic acid attacks it more easily
H+ is regenerated, so it is a catalyst and not used up

questions.question: The high-resolution 1H NMR spectrum of an ester is shown. Which is its skeletal formula? (Options not in text.)
questions.answer: D: ethyl 2,2-dimethylpropanoate, (CH3)3C-C(=O)-O-CH2CH3
steps: Three peaks with areas 9H, 3H and 2H: three hydrogen environments, 14 H in total
The 9H singlet at about 1.2 ppm is a (CH3)3C group (nine equivalent H with no neighbouring H)
The 2H quartet at about 4.1 ppm is OCH2 (next to a CH3) and the 3H triplet at about 1.2 ppm is the CH3 of the ethyl group
Only option D has C(CH3)3 and OCH2CH3 (option C would have the CH2 next to C=O at about 2.2 ppm, and a tert-butyl group on the oxygen)

questions.question: Name the reagents for Step 1 and Step 2 in the three-step synthesis of methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate from ethanal.
questions.answer: Step 1: HCN with KCN (cyanide ion catalyst); Step 2: dilute acid (H+/H2O) with heating (hydrolysis of the nitrile)
steps: Step 1 adds HCN to ethanal with CN- as the nucleophile, giving 2-hydroxypropanenitrile
Step 2 hydrolyses the nitrile group with dilute acid (and water) to the carboxylic acid
This gives 2-hydroxypropanoic acid, which is then esterified in Step 3

questions.question: Complete the mechanism for Step 1 (ethanal with cyanide), using curly arrows, lone pairs, charges and dipoles.
questions.answer: CN- attacks the delta+ carbonyl carbon, the C=O pi bond moves onto O to form an alkoxide, which is protonated by HCN to give the product and regenerate CN-
steps: Show the C=O bond dipole: C delta+, O delta-
Curly arrow from the lone pair on C in CN- to the carbonyl carbon
Curly arrow from the C=O pi bond onto O, giving O- (charge shown)
Curly arrow from H-CN onto O- to give the product and CN- again (catalytic)

questions.question: Explain why the 2-hydroxypropanoic acid produced in this synthesis is not optically active.
questions.answer: The product is a racemic mixture: CN- attacks the planar carbonyl from either side with equal probability, so equal amounts of the two enantiomers form and their rotations cancel
steps: The carbonyl carbon in ethanal is planar
CN- can attack from either face with equal probability
Equal amounts of the two enantiomers form, so the mixture is racemic
Opposite rotations of equal amounts cancel, so there is no net optical activity

questions.question: State the type of reaction in Step 3 (forming methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate).
questions.answer: Esterification (condensation reaction)
steps: Step 3 combines a carboxylic acid with an alcohol (methanol)
Water is eliminated, forming an ester: esterification (a condensation reaction)

questions.question: A small amount of a polymer forms during Step 3. Deduce the structure of the repeat unit of this polymer.
questions.answer: -[O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)]- (repeat unit of poly(2-hydroxypropanoic acid))
steps: The polymer forms by self-esterification of 2-hydroxypropanoic acid units
Each unit contributes -O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-
So the repeat unit is -O-CH(CH3)-CO-

questions.question: Label the displayed formula of methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate to show the protons responsible for peaks L (singlet, 1H) and M (singlet, 3H).
questions.answer: L = the OH proton (1H, singlet); M = the OCH3 protons (3H, singlet)
steps: Peak L is a singlet with 1 H: the OH proton has no adjacent C-H protons
Peak M is a singlet with 3 H: the OCH3 ester methyl has no adjacent C-H protons
Label the OH group as L and the -OCH3 group as M

questions.question: Complete the table giving the expected number of hydrogen atoms and splitting pattern for peaks J and K of methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate. (The table layout is shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: J: 3 hydrogen atoms, doublet; K: 1 hydrogen atom, quartet
steps: In methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate, CH3CH(OH)COOCH3, the CH3 attached to the CH is the 1.3 ppm peak J: 3 H
J is split by the one H on the neighbouring CH, so n + 1 = 2: a doublet
The CH (4.1 ppm, bonded to O and next to C=O) is the single-hydrogen environment K: 1 H, split by the 3 H of the CH3 into a quartet
L (1H, OH) and M (3H, OCH3) are singlets because they have no H on adjacent carbons

questions.question: Which isomer has the most peaks in its 13C NMR spectrum? (Options are in an image shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: C: 2-methylpentane, with 5 peaks in its 13C NMR spectrum
steps: Count the different carbon environments in each isomer (all are C6H14)
A (2,3-dimethylbutane) has 2 peaks, B (2,2-dimethylbutane) has 4 peaks, D (hexane) has 3 peaks
C (2-methylpentane, CH3CH2CH2CH(CH3)2) has 5 peaks: the two CH3 groups on the CH are equivalent, and the other four carbons are all different
So C has the most peaks

questions.question: Which compound has the most peaks in its 13C NMR spectrum? Options: A CH3COCH3, B CH3COCH2CH3, C CH3CH2COCH2CH3, D CH3COCH2CH2COCH3.
questions.answer: B (CH3COCH2CH3, butanone, 4 peaks)
steps: A (propanone) has 2 peaks: CH3 (2 equivalent) and C=O
B (butanone) has 4 peaks: CH3 next to C=O, C=O, CH2, CH3 of ethyl
C (pentan-3-one) has 3 peaks because its two ethyl groups are equivalent
D (hexane-2,5-dione) has 3 peaks because of its symmetry

questions.question: How many chiral centres are present in nandrolone? Options: A six, B seven, C eight, D nine.
questions.answer: A: six
steps: A chiral centre is a carbon atom bonded to four different groups
In nandrolone these are the ring-fusion carbons carrying an H (C8, C9, C10 and C14), the quaternary carbon bearing the methyl group (C13) and the carbon bearing OH (C17)
The C=C carbon (C5) and the C=O carbon (C3) are not chiral, so there are 6 chiral centres: option A

questions.question: Nandrolone is broken down in the body into a compound shown in the question. What reactions have taken place to form the new bonds at positions 1 and 2?
questions.answer: B: reduction at position 1 and addition at position 2
steps: At position 1 the C=O of the ketone in nandrolone has become a C-OH alcohol: reduction (gain of hydrogen)
At position 2 the C=C double bond has become a C-C single bond with an extra H on each carbon: addition (hydrogenation)
So the answer is reduction and addition: option B

questions.question: A sample with 2 x 10^-9 g cm-3 of nandrolone gives a chromatogram. Which chromatogram would be produced by a second sample at 4 x 10^-9 g cm-3 under the same conditions? (Chromatograms are shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: D: the peak at the same retention time (about 2.2 min) but about twice as tall
steps: In GC the retention time is a property of the compound under the same conditions, so the peak stays at about 2.2 min: only C and D qualify (A and B are at about 5 min)
The peak area (and height, for peaks of equal width) is proportional to the concentration, so doubling from 2 x 10^-9 to 4 x 10^-9 g cm-3 doubles the peak height
D shows the peak about twice the height of the original, while C is about the same as the original sample

questions.question: Calculate the atom economy, by mass, for the formation of oxalic acid from the hydrolysis of 2-oxobutanedioic acid.
steps: The equation is 2-oxobutanedioic acid + H2O -> ethanedioic acid (oxalic acid) + ethanoic acid
Mr of the products: oxalic acid 90 and ethanoic acid CH3COOH 60, total 150 (equal to the reactants: 132 + 18)
Atom economy = Mr of desired product / total Mr of products x 100 = 90 / 150 x 100 = 60%

questions.question: Give the laboratory reagents and conditions to convert glycolic acid, HOCH2COOH, to oxalic acid (nitric acid not considered).
questions.answer: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI) (K2Cr2O7/H2SO4), heated under reflux
steps: The CH2OH group is a primary alcohol and is oxidised to a carboxylic acid
Use an oxidising agent such as acidified K2Cr2O7 (or acidified KMnO4)
Heat under reflux with excess oxidant so the alcohol is fully oxidised to the acid

questions.topic: Oxidation of Sucrose by Nitric Acid
questions.question: Complete the equation for the reaction of one mole of sucrose with concentrated nitric acid to form oxalic acid.
steps: Products: oxalic acid (H2C2O4), NO2 (from HNO3 reduction) and H2O
C: 12 on each side gives 6 oxalic acid molecules
H and O balance gives 36 HNO3 and 23 H2O; N balances as 36 NO2

questions.question: Give one observation that would be seen during this reaction of sucrose with concentrated nitric acid.
questions.answer: Brown (orange-brown) fumes of NO2 are given off
steps: Concentrated HNO3 is reduced to NO2 in this reaction
NO2 is a brown gas, seen as brown fumes

questions.question: Select one indicator for each equivalence point from the titration graph of NaOH against oxalic acid, and give the colour at the end-point for each. Use the Data Booklet.
questions.answer: First equivalence point (25 cm3, pH rise about 2.7 to 4.6): methyl orange, orange at the end-point; second equivalence point (50 cm3, pH rise about 6.2 to 12.5): phenolphthalein, pale pink at the end-point
steps: The titration curve has two vertical sections: at 25 cm3 NaOH (first H+ neutralised) and at 50 cm3 (second H+ neutralised)
First: the steep part runs from about pH 2.7 to 4.6, so choose an indicator whose range lies in it, e.g. methyl orange (pH range about 3.1-4.4); end-point colour orange (red to yellow change)
Second: the steep part runs from about pH 6.2 to 12.5; phenolphthalein (range about 8.3-10.0) fits; end-point colour pale pink (colourless to pink)

questions.question: Suggest a difficulty that would occur if both indicators were present in the same mixture.
questions.answer: Their colour changes overlap, so the end-points cannot be distinguished clearly
steps: Each indicator changes colour over a pH range near its equivalence point
With both present, the colour changes overlap and blend
So it becomes hard to see each end-point separately

questions.question: Using the titration graph of NaOH with oxalic acid, determine the two Ka values for oxalic acid, showing working on the graph.
steps: Oxalic acid is diprotic and the equivalence points are at 25 cm3 and 50 cm3, so each stage of neutralisation uses 25 cm3
At half the first equivalence (12.5 cm3) [HA-] = [H2A], so Ka1 = [H+] and pH = pKa1: the graph reads pH about 1.3 at 12.5 cm3, so Ka1 = 10^-1.3 = 5 x 10^-2 mol dm-3
At half the second equivalence (37.5 cm3) [A2-] = [HA-], so pH = pKa2: the graph reads pH about 5.5 at 37.5 cm3
Ka2 = 10^-5.5 = 3.2 x 10^-6 mol dm-3; show the working by drawing vertical lines up from 12.5 and 37.5 cm3 to the curve and horizontal lines across to the pH axis

questions.question: Suggest how a pure sample of oxalic acid would be used to identify the oxalic acid peak in the HPLC chromatogram of the spinach extract.
questions.answer: Run the pure oxalic acid through the same HPLC; the peak with the same retention time is oxalic acid (or spike the extract and see which peak grows)
steps: Inject a pure sample of oxalic acid under the same conditions
Note its retention time on the detector trace
The peak in the spinach extract with the same retention time is oxalic acid

questions.topic: Mass of Spinach for Cleaning Solution
questions.question: A 0.558 mol dm-3 oxalic acid cleaning solution (500 cm3) is to be made from spinach that gives about 700 mg oxalic acid per 100 g. Calculate the mass of spinach required. (Mr oxalic acid = 90.)
questions.answer: About 3590 g (3.6 kg) of spinach
steps: Moles of oxalic acid = 0.558 x 0.500 = 0.279 mol
Mass of oxalic acid = 0.279 x 90 = 25.1 g
Spinach needed: 0.700 g oxalic acid per 100 g spinach, so mass = 25.1 / 0.700 x 100 = 3590 g

questions.question: Write the equation for the reaction of oxalic acid with excess phosphorus(V) chloride.
questions.answer: (COOH)2 + 2PCl5 -> (COCl)2 + 2POCl3 + 2HCl
steps: Carboxylic acid -COOH is converted to acyl chloride -COCl by PCl5
Each PCl5 gives POCl3 and HCl as by-products
Balance: C 2 and H 2 (= 2 HCl) on each side; O 4 (2 in (COCl)2 plus 2 in 2 POCl3); P 2; Cl 10 (2 + 6 + 2)

questions.topic: NMR and MS of Propanal and Propanone
questions.question: Discuss the similarities and differences in the proton NMR and mass spectra of propanal and propanone, including number of peaks, relative peak areas, splitting patterns, and one similarity and one difference in m/z peaks.
questions.answer: Propanal: 3 peaks (1:2:3, CHO triplet, CH2 multiplet, CH3 triplet); propanone: 1 singlet (6H). Both have M+ = 58; propanone has a base peak at m/z 43 (CH3CO+), propanal shows m/z 29 (C2H5+) and 57 (M-H)
steps: NMR: propanal gives three peaks in the ratio 1:2:3 (CHO, CH2, CH3)
Propanal's CHO proton is a triplet and the CH3 a triplet, showing neighbouring CH2 coupling
Propanone gives one peak (singlet, 6H) since both CH3 are equivalent
MS: both have molecular ion peak at m/z 58 (similarity)
Propanone gives a base peak at m/z 43 (CH3CO+), while propanal gives m/z 29 (C2H5+) and 57 (loss of H)

questions.question: An organic compound X has a molecular ion at m/z = 60.0210 (H 1.0078, C 12.0000, N 14.0031, O 15.9949). Which compound is X? Options: A CH3CH2CH2OH, B CH3COOH, C CO(NH2)2, D (CH3)3N.
questions.answer: B (CH3COOH, C2H4O2)
steps: So X is CH3COOH

questions.question: Four ester isomers of C4H8O2 are shown. Explain which one can be distinguished from the other three by the number of peaks in its 13C NMR spectrum, labelling equivalent carbons.
questions.answer: 1-methylethyl (isopropyl) methanoate, HCOOCH(CH3)2, which gives 3 peaks (the two CH3 carbons are equivalent); the other three esters give 4 peaks each
steps: The four esters are ethyl ethanoate, methyl propanoate, propyl methanoate and 1-methylethyl methanoate
Ethyl ethanoate, methyl propanoate and propyl methanoate each have four different carbon environments: 4 peaks
1-methylethyl methanoate, HCOOCH(CH3)2, has two equivalent CH3 carbons, so only 3 peaks
Therefore 1-methylethyl methanoate is the one distinguished by its number of peaks

questions.topic: Low Resolution NMR of C5H10O2 Esters
questions.question: Esters W and X (C5H10O2) each have one peak with relative area 3 in their low-resolution 1H NMR spectra. Explain how these peaks can be used to distinguish the two esters.
questions.answer: Compare the chemical shifts of the 3H peaks: in W the 3H peak (OCH3) is at about 3.6-3.7 ppm, in X the 3H peak (CH3 on C=O) is at about 2.0-2.1 ppm
steps: W is methyl 2-methylpropanoate, (CH3)2CHCOOCH3: its 3H peak is the OCH3, a CH3 bonded to an oxygen, at about 3.6-3.7 ppm (range about 2.9-4.2 ppm)
X is propan-2-yl ethanoate, CH3COOCH(CH3)2: its 3H peak is the CH3 bonded to the C=O, at about 2.0-2.1 ppm (range about 2.1-2.7 ppm)
The two 3H peaks therefore appear at different chemical shifts, so the esters can be told apart

questions.question: Label the displayed formulae of two different C5H10O2 esters with their proton environments, clearly indicating equivalent environments, and describe the splitting patterns of their high-resolution 1H NMR spectra.
questions.answer: Y (butan-2-yl methanoate, HCOOCH(CH3)CH2CH3): HCO singlet (1H); OCH sextet (1H); CH2 quintet (2H); CH3 on the CH doublet (3H); CH3 of the ethyl group triplet (3H). Z (2-methylpropyl methanoate, HCOOCH2CH(CH3)2): HCO singlet (1H); OCH2 doublet (2H); CH multiplet of 9 peaks (1H); two equivalent CH3 doublet (6H)
steps: Label each different hydrogen environment on the displayed formulae with a letter, giving the same letter to equivalent H (e.g. the two CH3 groups of the CH(CH3)2 in Z)

Y has five environments: H-C(=O)O singlet (no neighbours); O-CH next to CH3 (3H) and CH2 (2H), so 5 neighbours, a sextet (6 peaks); CH2 next to CH (1) and CH3 (3), 4 neighbours, a quintet; CH3 on the CH, 1 neighbour, a doublet; CH3 of the ethyl group, 2 neighbours, a triplet

Z has four environments: H-C(=O)O singlet; OCH2 next to a single CH, a doublet; CH next to CH2 (2H) and two CH3 (6H), so 8 neighbours, a multiplet of 9 peaks; the two equivalent CH3 groups (6H) next to the CH, a doublet
Relative areas for Y are 1 : 1 : 2 : 3 : 3 and for Z are 1 : 2 : 1 : 6

questions.topic: Ester with Only Two NMR Peaks
questions.question: Draw the displayed formula of the C5H10O2 ester which has only 2 peaks in its low-resolution 1H NMR spectrum.
questions.answer: HCOOC(CH3)3 (tert-butyl methanoate)
steps: The only environments must be the CHO proton (1H) and the nine equivalent CH3 protons (9H)
The ester with this arrangement is methanoate of tert-butyl alcohol: HCOOC(CH3)3
Its formula is C5H10O2, with two peaks (1H and 9H)

questions.question: A thin-layer chromatogram of a substance is shown. What is its Rf value? Options: A 0.27, B 0.69, C 0.73, D 1.37.
